name: Publishing the decision record
summary: You run the publish command; the record is validated, written to docs/decisions/, indexed, and merged via git review.

steps.label: Decide to publish
steps.description: You decide to publish by running the command the staging notice printed, from any shell and folder, or by asking Claude Code to run it and open a pull request.

approval.note: approved_at is the decision's updated_at: the kernel Decision had no approved_at field when this decision was approved (added by #KernelDecisionStore).

steps.label: Validate the staged record
steps.description: The publish command checks the staged record's structure and links, and that its components and roadmap phase appear in the project's component list and roadmap.

approval.note: approved_at is the decision's updated_at: the kernel Decision had no approved_at field when this decision was approved (added by #KernelDecisionStore).

steps.label: Write the record and the index
steps.description: The publish command writes the record into the decision folder of the kernel checkout and regenerates the decision index.

approval.note: approved_at is the decision's updated_at: the kernel Decision had no approved_at field when this decision was approved (added by #KernelDecisionStore).

steps.label: Validate the store
steps.description: The validate command checks the whole decision store and reports any problems it finds.

approval.note: approved_at is the decision's updated_at: the kernel Decision had no approved_at field when this decision was approved (added by #KernelDecisionStore).

steps.label: Commit and review in git
steps.description: The new record and index are committed, and a pull request is opened and reviewed like any other change, because Git is the canonical store.

approval.note: approved_at is the decision's updated_at: the kernel Decision had no approved_at field when this decision was approved (added by #KernelDecisionStore).

steps.label: Merge to main
steps.description: The pull request merges to main, and from then on every later run working from that revision can find the record.

approval.note: approved_at is the decision's updated_at: the kernel Decision had no approved_at field when this decision was approved (added by #KernelDecisionStore).

branches.label: Keep it staged
branches.description: The record stays only in the run folder, so later runs, which look up precedent through the published index, never find it.

approval.note: approved_at is the decision's updated_at: the kernel Decision had no approved_at field when this decision was approved (added by #KernelDecisionStore).

branches.condition: the run has no staged decision record
branches.label: Exit 3: no staged record
branches.description: The publish command stops with an error naming the run, writes no file and leaves the index untouched.

examples.label: Illustrative failed publish: no staged record

problems.message: no staged decision record for this run

branches.condition: a component or roadmap phase on the record is not in docs/components.json or docs/roadmap.json
branches.label: Exit 3: unknown filter value
branches.description: The publish command stops, names the unknown component or roadmap phase, and writes nothing until the record uses known values.

examples.label: Illustrative model-valid filter rejected by repository vocabulary checks
Illustrative refused publish with invalid component; diagnostic wording illustrative

branches.condition: you pass --correct OLD_ID for an older record that the new record supersedes
branches.label: Correct an older record
branches.description: The publish command marks the older record as corrected and superseded by the new one, keeps its original choice, evidence and assumptions, and rewrites it in one safe step.

examples.label: Counterfactual after explicit correction; synthetic new record id, not stored

corrections.reason: Illustrative future correction after a new human decision.

acceptance_scenarios.given: a staged decision record and the publish instruction
acceptance_scenarios.then: you run the printed publish command (<python> <repo_root>/scripts/run_kernel.py decisions publish --run-id R) as shown, or Claude Code runs it at your request and opens a PR

acceptance_scenarios.given: a staged record for run R
acceptance_scenarios.then: its schema, links, and component and roadmap filter values are checked against docs/components.json and docs/roadmap.json before anything is written

acceptance_scenarios.given: a staged record that passed validation
acceptance_scenarios.then: docs/decisions/<id>.yaml exists and docs/decisions/index.json is regenerated to include it

acceptance_scenarios.given: a newly written record and index

acceptance_scenarios.then: a PR is opened and reviewed in git like any other change
the record is on main and every later run can find it through the index

acceptance_scenarios.when: you choose not to publish it
acceptance_scenarios.then: it stays in the run folder only and no later run finds it as precedent

acceptance_scenarios.given: a run with no staged decision record
acceptance_scenarios.when: python -m kernel decisions publish --run-id R runs
acceptance_scenarios.then: it exits 3 with "no staged decision record for this run" and writes nothing

acceptance_scenarios.given: a staged record whose component or roadmap phase is not in the vocabularies
acceptance_scenarios.then: it exits 3 naming the unknown value and writes nothing

acceptance_scenarios.given: a staged record that supersedes an older published record
acceptance_scenarios.then: the older record gets a correction and superseded_by appended, and none of its existing content is changed

provenance.note: Sub-flow 3 of leafcutter/decision-lifecycle (kernel decision dec-5e7445182eaec1f2): a human-run publish command, then git review. Exit codes and --correct checked against kernel/memory/cli.py and publish.py on main.
Migrated every node to source-backed checked handoffs and labeled examples; preserved runtime, approvals and AC status.

Updated decide-to-publish to the runnable publish command the staged notice now prints (PR #999): the kernel's own interpreter with scripts/run_kernel.py, and the named docs/decisions folder. Prose and that scenario only; the publish CLI, its JSON result schema, contract bindings, approvals and AC links are unchanged.
